clue.text: Comfort of notable fifth brilliant service

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi, fa, sol) the fifth note is sol: a fifth that is a note
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: Praise for some celebrated fifth player's dazzling serve at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notable' splits as note-able: the fifth note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation, the comfort given to someone in distress.

clue.text: It provides iron for chaps in trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disorder, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Something that offers strength to men in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' suggests golf or laundry; it is the mineral the vegetable is famed for, as with Popeye.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy vegetable famous for being rich in iron.

clue.text: Language lately starts to be fashionable

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, here the beginning of the word lately

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A language that has recently begun to come into vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the language of ancient Rome.

clue.text: With 2, playwright gets a tip

parts.note: with in 2-down, Latin, is cum
George Bernard Shaw was the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A dramatist alongside a Roman receives a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer at 2-down, LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumshaw is pidgin from Chinese ports for a gratuity or tip.

clue.text: Caller providing a solution

definitions.meaning: one who rings, a bell-... or someone telephoning
... solution is the saline fluid used in medicine, named after Sydney ...

explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer or telephoner calls; Ringer's solution is a named medical saline fluid.

clue.text: It's sin … perhaps you could twist my arm!

indicators.note: perhaps suggests an alternative version, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Admitting a temptation is wrong while hinting you would give in under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to press a demand, the arm-twisting persuasion the phrase describes.

clue.text: Element seen by many in bloom

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a geranium is a flowering plant
M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many

explanation.surface: A chemical seen by crowds in a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanium is a chemical element, a metalloid used in semiconductors.

clue.text: Rapidly announce cancellation of dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
something off is cancelled

explanation.surface: Quickly declaring that a dance is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off is to recite a list quickly and fluently.

clue.text: Severe sense of guilt for drink in the case of a detective

parts.note: bitter is a British draught beer
re means concerning or in the case of
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels

explanation.surface: A detective drowning his guilt in drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter remorse is a harsh, painful regret, an acute sense of guilt.

clue.text: It's said to be unseen through this

definitions.text: It's said to be unseen through this

indicators.note: said marks that the word for unseen is heard, not written

parts.note: something unseen has been missed

explanation.surface: A riddle about what you cannot see through.
explanation.walkthrough: Things go missed, unseen, when you look through the fog-like vapour the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a thin fog through which objects go unseen.

clue.text: Deal soundly with public utility infrastructure in a big way

parts.note: the mains are the network of pipes and cables carrying gas, water and electricity

indicators.note: soundly here means as it sounds, so the word for deal is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to deal with something is to treat it

explanation.surface: Advice on handling the pipes and cables of the utilities on a grand scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals that TREAT is only heard, spelt TREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A main street is the principal thoroughfare of a town, its biggest road.

clue.text: Start consuming a meal

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Beginning by eating some food.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a venture is to start it off.

clue.text: One devises treats to gather for later distribution

indicators.note: distribution spreads things around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks up treats to collect and hand out later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devises' is the legal verb: to leave land by will, not to invent.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator makes a will, and to devise is to bequeath property by will.

clue.text: Web theory as applied in Manhattan

indicators.note: a theory as applied is put into practice and reshaped, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Internet theory put into practice in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bowery is a street and district on Manhattan's Lower East Side.

clue.text: Old reporter reported for drink

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for drink is heard

parts.note: a beverage is a drink

explanation.surface: A former journalist said to be in for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reporter' is not a journalist: William BEVERIDGE wrote the 1942 Beveridge Report founding Britain's welfare state.
explanation.definitionFit: William Beveridge authored the famous 1942 Beveridge Report, so he is a reporter from history.

clue.text: Spat at breakfast place lacking any point

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so letters are taken away

parts.note: Breakfast at Tiffany's is the Truman Capote novella and Audrey Hepburn film
taken as written
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone spat at a breakfast spot that had no point.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, a spat.

clue.text: Wild party in Gloucester Avenue

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words Gloucester Avenue

explanation.surface: A riotous party held in a street in Gloucester.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large, lively dance party, a wild party.

clue.text: Trusting in the Spanish train design

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
design means arrangement, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Faith in the layout of Spanish railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train design' reads as railway engineering; 'design' makes RIANT, and 'in' places the Spanish article inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliant means dependent on, trusting in someone or something.

clue.text: Heroine's end made so troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: The heroine's ending made so distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is the heroine of Shakespeare's Othello, whose end is tragic.

clue.text: Low water could be eased without notice

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
could be suggests the letters may form something else

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: Tension that could be relieved without any warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low water' suggests a tide; 'could be' makes DESEA, and 'without' wraps it round the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea lies at the lowest land elevation on Earth, so it is the lowest water.

clue.text: Nice top job for one in the family

indicators.note: a job here is a fix or piece of work, so these letters are worked over

explanation.surface: A plum post handed to a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotic describes favouritism shown to relatives, as in nepotism.

clue.text: Claim right in a property

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an asset is a piece of property

explanation.surface: Asserting a right to a piece of real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to claim or state forcefully.

clue.text: Coal fires? One's not needed working outside

indicators.note: working means operating in a new arrangement, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not needed means dropped, so a letter is removed

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: No need for a coal fire when you work outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not needed' removes I (one) from COALFIRES, leaving COALFRES; 'working' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, outside.

clue.text: Receive legislation about fungus

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an act is a piece of legislation
a cep is an edible mushroom, the porcini

explanation.surface: Getting a law passed concerning mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to take or receive it.

clue.text: Capability, say, without lands to frolic

indicators.note: without means minus, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Capability Brown was the great English landscape gardener, an example of a landscaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden designer shorn of estates leaps about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capability' looks like ability; it names Capability Brown, the eighteenth-century English landscape gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip and frolic playfully.

clue.text: Battle clothing once found in Holloway

parts.note: a battle is war in miniature
dresses are items of clothing

explanation.surface: Combat outfits that used to be seen in a London prison.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLLOWAY was a women's prison in London; 'once' marks the old word for female prison officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardresses were female prison warders, staffing women's jails like Holloway.

clue.text: Ruth unknown by mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Ruth, a stranger beside the mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' poses as a name; it is the old word for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic word for compassion, the root of ruthless.

clue.text: Take sustenance in attempt to come to agreement

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to take sustenance is to eat

explanation.surface: Eat while trying to reach a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: Material for some of the fabulously rich?

parts.note: fab is the slang shortening of fabulous

indicators.note: some of means only part, so the word rich loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cloth suited to the very wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' trims the H from RICH; FAB is the slang clipping of fabulous, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, textile material.
